children: The FDA approved AstraZeneca’s perioperative IMFINZI plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin-ejfv regimen for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are ineligible for or have refused cisplatin. In VOLGA, it reduced EFS risk by 49% and death risk by 42% versus the comparator.
FDA approved regimen for cisplatin-ineligible MIBC
Adds a US-approved treatment option for a patient group that may represent up to half of MIBC patients.
The Phase III result supports the regimen’s clinical case; estimated median EFS was not reached versus 12.1 months.
Overall-survival results strengthen the evidence for the regimen; median OS was not reached in either arm.
Higher severe adverse-event incidence than the comparator is a relevant trade-off for uptake and treatment decisions.
EU, Japan and other applications remain under review
Additional decisions could broaden the commercial opportunity, but timing and outcomes were not specified.

This is a third bladder cancer indication for IMFINZI in two years, extending the drug’s role into cisplatin-ineligible MIBC. Further regulatory decisions in the EU, Japan and other countries would be the next catalyst for broader adoption.
